title: Four times farther: how much gravity?
hook: Move a spacecraft farther from a spherical planet.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Outside a spherical mass, gravitational acceleration is GM/r². Four times the distance gives 4² = 16 times the denominator, so the acceleration is one sixteenth.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Outside a spherical mass, gravitational acceleration is GM/r². Four times the distance gives 4² = 16 times the denominator, so the acceleration is one sixteenth.

claims.text: Outside a spherical mass, gravitational acceleration is GM/r². Four times the distance gives 4² = 16 times the denominator, so the acceleration is one sixteenth. Spherical planet, outside its surface; ignore other gravitating bodies. Distance is measured from the centre.
claims.source: Newtonian gravitational field g = GM/r² outside a spherically symmetric mass.

recall.question: At twice the distance from the centre of a spherical planet, what is its gravitational acceleration relative to before?
recall.why: g scales as 1/r², so doubling distance gives one quarter.
